newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf gas prices sink on temps, storage concerns.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf gas prices sink on temps, storage concerns.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices at the Gulf skidded more than 15 cents Thursday, with mostly above-normal U.S. weather this week and concerns about stocks, particularly in the East, weighed on the market, industry sources said.
While Wednesday's overall AGA stock report was seen as neutral, traders said the rising surplus in the East, now 153 bcf or 23 percent over last year, was a growing concern.

"We haven't seen a lot of cold this month and there are a lot of LDCs (utilities) looking to exchange gas now for summer supply," said a Midwest trader, noting Gulf Coast swing prices were mostly in the mid-to-high $2.40s, 40 cents below index.
Prices in south Texas also lost ground, with gas on Tetco quoted in the mid-to-high $2.30s, off more than five cents on the day and 30 cents below Feb 1 levels.

While forecasts for Texas next week were mixed, most agreed prices there would remain vulnerable to weather-related spikes, with producing region stocks still more than 15 percent below year-ago, according to recent AGA data.
In west Texas, Permian prices were in the mid-$2.30s, down several cents on the day and more than 20 cents below first of the month levels.
In the Midwest, prices slumped more than a dime to the mid-to-high $2.30s, about 35 cents below index.
In the East, expectations for cooler temperatures by early next week helped hold New York city-gate prices relatively steady in the low-$3.00 area.
Swing prices at the southern California border were pegged slightly lower at about $2.50.
